claim_scope: RouteReleaseRegistryV1 provides one bounded canonical and fail-closed mapping from a command-variant root plus a lane-sorted module-release set to one exact RouteReleaseV1, rejects ambiguity, fallback, noncanonical input, and exact module-registry union mismatches, and grants no profile or route-execution authority.
failure_modes: a registry accepts zero or more than 256 routes
a selector accepts zero or more than eight module releases
a selector admits duplicate or noncanonical lane order
duplicate route IDs or duplicate command-and-release selection keys are admitted
route iteration order silently determines a winner
an unknown command or release set falls back to another route
a route change does not change the registry root
a missing, extra, reordered, duplicate-lane, or wrong-release module registry union binds
empty, oversized, trailing, stale, reordered, unknown-field, over-count, or noncanonical registry input decodes
a RouteReleaseRegistry source or test is omitted from the governed ZRPF source closure

aaa.reason: Rust contract tests use explicit Arrange, Act, and Assert phases for registry and selector cardinality, canonical order, ambiguity, exact lookup, registry binding, identity, and codec behavior; the isolated pytest launcher asserts the exact 12-test Rust result.

reject_is_noop.reason: Construction, lookup, and module-registry binding operate on immutable caller-owned values; selector-order and unknown-lookup tests preserve the complete input or registry before and after rejection, and no method exposes mutable committed state.

mutations.description: accept zero or more than 256 registry routes or zero or more than eight selector dependencies
accept duplicate or reversed selector lanes or silently normalize caller selection input
admit duplicate route IDs, ambiguous selection keys, or more than one canonical registry permutation
fall back from an unknown command or module release set to another registered route
bind a missing, extra, reordered, duplicate-lane, or wrong-release module registry union
omit a route identity from the registry root or accept stale, nonminimal, unknown-field, trailing, empty, oversized, reordered, or over-count input
omit a RouteReleaseRegistry implementation or assurance source from the exact ZRPF inventory

nonclaims: RouteSelectionKeyV1 is ordinary caller-constructible data. This packet does not derive it from an authenticated command, committed object pins, or a governed EconomicProfileSnapshotV1 and does not construct an authority witness.

Exact lookup proves only that one registry contains one route for the supplied command root and lane-sorted module release set. It does not select lifecycle purpose, authenticate profile activation, consume a nonce or object, or establish replay uniqueness.

Exact module-registry union binding proves record occurrence only. It does not reinterpret release lifecycle status, prove coexistence economics, migration, terminal execution, or resource consumption.

This packet does not inspect module receipts or private-port values, compose a route proof, verify an epoch, authorize ZenoLedger publication, establish complete M6 route coverage, production readiness, whole-economy authority, or ShapeForge promoted-bundle status.
